paragraphs: FMX sells facilities and maintenance management software that organizations use to streamline processes and get more out of their assets. For cities and counties, the pitch is maximizing asset performance, allocating spaces and funding, and streamlining resident service delivery. A school edition promises facility management software that will meet a district where it is at.

Work order management streamlines request submissions and helps staff resolve maintenance issues. Preventive maintenance handles compliance and schedules recurring tasks. Reporting tracks labor hours and costs so investments can be justified. Separate products cover vehicles, keeping a fleet on the road and tracking repairs. The products are cloud-based. A 14-day free trial is offered.

The company says it serves over 400K professionals. Beyond schools it sells into public works, covering public infrastructure, assets, public property, capital projects, and community events. It points to 400+ reviews on Capterra, Software Advice, and G2. Pricing turns on how many users an organization has, or the number of students enrolled for public K-12 schools.

quote.text: Easy for technicians in the field. Powerful for leaders behind the scenes. One system to get everyone on the same page.
